correctness.rationale: The bounding-box area is w_n(theta)w_n(theta+pi/2), the product of two perpendicular support-function widths. Reduction of the nearest-vertex phase modulo 2pi/n for even n and modulo pi/n for odd n gives a uniform cosine phase with (C,D,b)=(2R^2,1,2pi/n) for 4|n; (2R^2,cos(pi/n),pi/n) for n=2 mod 4; and (2R^2 cos^2(pi/(2n)),cos(pi/(2n)),pi/(2n)) for n odd. These identities hold for n=3,4 and all larger n without degeneracy. Uniform |T| in [0,b] proves the arccos CDF on the exact interval and zero endpoint atoms. Integrating cos(T), cos^2(T) establishes exact moments. Since Var(cos T)=b^4/45+O(b^6), the n^4/R^4 variance limits are 64pi^4/45, 4pi^4/45, pi^4/180, hence 256:16:1. For X=(U-B)/(U-L), the arcsin CDF yields a uniform b-expansion; maximizing sqrt(x)-x^(3/2) at x=1/3 gives sharp b^2/(36sqrt(3)) Kolmogorov correction. Independent Cartesian vertex-width quadrature checked 12 n cases, orientation samples, and moments, independent of the source phase code. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove universal n.
residual_risks: Sharp Kolmogorov coefficient follows from a uniform expansion, not finite CDF sampling; independent quadrature tests only finite n.

value.rationale: Random orientation versus optimal placement is a genuine geometric-probability distinction: this all-n law quantifies uncertainty in standard axis-aligned bounding rectangles. The arithmetic mod-four fluctuation hierarchy and exact universal normalized loss law are natural sharp invariants, not arbitrary sampled values.
residual_risks: Novelty, correctness and reproducibility alone do not establish value; here the mathematical purpose and natural invariant are separately articulated.

final_claim: For each regular n-gon (n>=3) of circumradius R>0 rotated with Haar uniform orientation, its Cartesian bounding box area is exactly C_n(D_n+cos T_n), T_n uniform on [-b_n,b_n], with explicit mod-four parameters; the exact CDF and moments give three variance constants in ratio 256:16:1, and normalized area loss converges to Beta(1/2,1) with sharp Kolmogorov leading correction.
limitations: The result is for random uniform orientation of a fixed regular polygon and a Cartesian, axis-aligned bounding rectangle, not for optimization over all surrounding rectangles.
Unindexed prior probability formula remains possible; no publication with unsanitized public metadata.
